methodology: MVP: Sleeper player search rank + actual league production (when available) + roster fit + starting-lineup impact.
headline: Brae Wins the Fit Battle in a Balanced Swap
verdict: Brae is the current winner, with the stronger overall grade and a major roster-fit edge.
summary: This is a remarkably balanced package by the supplied heuristic values: Parker receives 162.7 in player value, while Brae receives 167.0. The grades separate the deal more clearly than the raw totals. Parker lands a B-, with 84 roster fit and 86 lineup impact, while Brae earns a B through an outstanding 93.5 roster-fit score and the same 86 lineup-impact mark. Smith-Njigba brings the highest individual value in the trade, but Chase Brown’s 26 recent average gives Brae a compelling production piece alongside Jefferson. At 5-9, Brae gets the better current grade; Parker’s 8-6 team remains a plausible counterweight. Even Public Enemy Parker did not turn this into another dogshit trade.

sides.analysis: Parker’s return is headlined by Jaxon Smith-Njigba, whose 98.3 value, sixth search rank, 20.3 season average, and 19.4 recent average make him the trade’s strongest individual asset. Bucky Irving adds a running back with a 64.4 value and steady 7.5 season and 7.8 recent averages. The package fits an 8-6 roster carrying six running backs and four wideouts, while the 86 lineup-impact score says the swap can matter immediately. The principal concern is surrendering Chase Brown, whose 93.7 value and 26 recent average are the deal’s hottest production profile.
sides.bestReason: Smith-Njigba is the highest-value player involved, and Parker’s six-RB/four-WR roster can absorb the positional reshuffle.
sides.biggestRisk: Giving up Chase Brown’s 26 recent average could sting if his recent production remains the strongest part of this package.
